environment.method_note: All mutating tests ran against a git clone at $SCRATCH/repo-copy, reset with 'git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -qfd' between cases. The source repo was mutated exactly once (rebuild-index.py writes in place, item 2) and restored immediately with 'git checkout -- .claude/devlog/index.json'.

summary: All four pieces of live machinery execute and their guards genuinely fire. Three shipped runtime claims re-derived independently and reproduce, one to the exact result count. Findings: (a) release.sh accepts any string as a version — no format validation; (b) release.sh's shipped-by stamp guard is bypassed by a multi-commit release; (c) index.json is NOT byte-identical across runs — 'generated_at' changes every invocation, so the repo's own reindex always dirties the tree; (d) the drift detector's own count has risen 18 -> 20 since v1.19.0, i.e. it is signalling drift right now, and the two new hits sit in a file whose header pin contradicts its own body; (e) one published sub-claim is REFUTED: the failing WebSearch tool_result DOES carry is_error:true.

items.name: plugins/harness/scripts/release.sh — release guard
what_it_actually_checks: writes <version> into BOTH plugins' plugin.json (lockstep is enforced by construction, not by comparison)
marketplace drift: fails if any entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json declares a 'version' key
shipped-by stamps: every file in plugins/harness/references/project-docs/*.md that is modified-vs-HEAD or untracked must carry 'shipped-by: claude-code-harness v<version>' on line 1
tag v<version> must not already exist
stages the shippable surface; deliberately does not commit

cases.observed: version: harness=1.20.0  devlog=1.20.0  (lockstep; marketplace carries no version, by design) / staged both plugin.json / EXIT=0
cases.result: pass (control — the guard is reachable and does not false-positive)

cases.observed: MARKETPLACE DRIFT: a plugin entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json declares 'version' — remove it (plugin.json is authoritative). EXIT=1

cases.note: The plugin.json files are rewritten BEFORE this check runs, so a rejected run still leaves the working tree modified. Cosmetic, not a correctness hole (the script never commits), but it means a failed release.sh must be followed by a git checkout.

cases.observed: version: harness=banana  devlog=banana ... EXIT=0; jq -r .version plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json -> "banana"; printed handoff says 'git tag vbanana'
cases.finding: release.sh performs zero validation of the version argument. Any string is written into both plugin.json files and echoed into the commit/tag commands. Since plugin.json's version is the consumers' update cache key (the script's own header says so), a malformed or backwards version ships silently. A semver regex on $V before the jq write would close this in one line.

cases.case: T6 project-doc modified without stamp bump
cases.observed: STAMP MISMATCH: plugins/harness/references/project-docs/docs-discipline.md is modified but its header is not 'shipped-by: claude-code-harness v1.20.0' / Fix the stamps above, then re-run. / EXIT=1

cases.case: T7 project-doc modified WITH stamp bumped
cases.result: pass (negative control — the stamp guard is not a blanket refusal)
GUARD FIRES (head -1 is strict about line 1 — intended, and it does not silently pass)
pass — a desynced devlog plugin.json is overwritten, so lockstep cannot be violated by the script's own path

cases.case: HOLE PROBE — stamp guard vs a multi-commit release
cases.command: printf '\nunstamped edit\n' >> plugins/harness/references/project-docs/docs-discipline.md; git commit -qam 'wip: earlier commit of this release'; bash plugins/harness/scripts/release.sh 1.20.0
cases.observed: version: harness=1.20.0 devlog=1.20.0 / Staged. / EXIT=0 — NO stamp mismatch reported, while the file's line-1 stamp still read v1.10.1
cases.control: The identical edit left UNCOMMITTED does produce 'STAMP MISMATCH: ...docs-discipline.md' — so the probe method is sound and the difference is the commit, not the edit.
cases.finding: The stamp check keys on 'git diff --quiet HEAD -- $f'. If a project-doc is edited and committed in an earlier commit of the same release cycle, HEAD already contains the edit, the diff is empty, and the file is never stamp-checked — a stale shipped-by stamp ships. This is exactly the class of defect release.sh was written to mechanize away (its header cites 'shipped-by stamps pointing at versions that exist in no commit'). Currently latent rather than live: the repo's release ritual runs release.sh before the single release commit. Closing it would mean diffing against the previous tag (git diff --quiet <last-tag> -- $f) instead of HEAD.

items.name: plugins/devlog/skills/devlog/rebuild-index.py — reindexer/validator

idempotence.observed: index.json + tldr.md updated: 30 entries (devlog root: /home/nikita/PROJECTS/claude-code-harness/.claude/devlog) / EXIT=0
idempotence.index_json: NOT byte-identical — REFUTES the stated expectation
idempotence.normalized_check: jq 'del(.generated_at)' before | diff - after  ->  IDENTICAL modulo generated_at
idempotence.finding: index.json embeds a wall-clock 'generated_at' stamp, so every invocation of the repo's own reindexer produces a one-line diff on a committed, generated artifact ('M .claude/devlog/index.json') even when no entry changed. Content-wise the committed artifacts ARE in sync with entries/ — the delta is purely the timestamp. Practical cost: the devlog ritual cannot be run as a no-op verification (e.g. 'reindex and confirm clean tree'), and every devlog commit carries a spurious timestamp churn line. Either drop generated_at or exclude it from the tree-clean check.
idempotence.restoration: git checkout -- .claude/devlog/index.json (repo returned to as-found; verified with git diff --stat HEAD -> empty)

validator_cases.method: fresh scratch devlog at $SCRATCH/dl with one known-good entry; each case re-created the baseline then introduced exactly one defect
validator_cases.V0_baseline_control: PASS — 'index.json + tldr.md updated: 1 entries', EXIT=0 (proves the harness accepts a valid entry, so the rejections below are not a blanket failure)
validator_cases.V2_duplicate_id: REJECTED — 'duplicate id 1: entries/0001-first-entry.md vs entries/0001-second-entry.md', EXIT=1
validator_cases.V4_no_frontmatter: REJECTED — 'entries/0003-naked.md: missing or malformed frontmatter', EXIT=1
validator_cases.V5_id_filename_mismatch: REJECTED — 'entries/0009-mismatch-id.md: frontmatter id 7 != filename id 9', EXIT=1
validator_cases.V6_filename_not_NNNN_slug: REJECTED — 'entries/no-number.md: filename must match NNNN-slug pattern', EXIT=1
validator_cases.V7_no_artifacts_on_error: CONFIRMED — after a failing run, 'ls $SCRATCH/dl' showed only 'entries'; neither index.json nor tldr.md was written, so a rejected run cannot publish a half-valid index

items.conclusion: It is a real validator: 6/6 seeded defects rejected with exit 1 and a specific message, artifacts withheld on error, and a passing control. The only refuted element is the byte-identity expectation for index.json.

items.name: Drift detector (v1.19.0) — references/audit-checklist.md §1
items.location: plugins/harness/references/audit-checklist.md, §1 'Stale model / version pins', bullet 'Run the drift detector — the class, not the case'

cases.case: needle control (validate the method before trusting a count)
cases.observed: 58 raw hits inside the inventory; 0 survive the allowlist
cases.result: method validated — the regex genuinely matches version pins, and the allowlist genuinely suppresses the inventory
DETECTOR IS SIGNALLING — the checklist's own rule is 'a rising hit count between audits is the drift signal'; 18 -> 20 over seven releases in one day

cases.case: D1 — inject the drift it claims to detect, into a LIVE doc
cases.command: printf '\nGrounded for Opus 4.7, Claude Code v2.1.199.\n' >> plugins/harness/SKILL.md; <detector> | wc -l
cases.observed: 21 (was 20); survivor listed as 'plugins/harness/SKILL.md:208:Grounded for Opus 4.7, Claude Code v2.1.199.'

cases.command: append the same line to CHANGELOG.md and .claude/devlog/tldr.md; <detector> | wc -l
cases.result: correctly suppressed — the allowlist protects provenance layers as designed

cases.case: D3 — pin injected into the INVENTORY itself (must NOT raise)

cases.result: correctly suppressed — the single version-carrying doc is exempt by design

cases.case: D4 — identify the two NEW survivors since v1.19.0
observed: plugins/harness/references/harness-discipline.md: '- **The effort tier.** On Opus 5, `xhigh`/`max` kill `WebSearch`, and a delegate that declares'
plugins/harness/references/harness-discipline.md: '  `claude-fable-5`, which keep search at `xhigh` and `max` — the two tiers that break Opus 5.'
cases.result: the drift is real and localised

items.finding: The detector works on every axis tested — it fires on injected live-doc drift, stays silent on frozen layers and on the inventory, and its recorded baseline of 18 reproduces exactly. What it is currently reporting is a genuine, unremediated condition, and the target form named in the same section ('exactly one file carries the currency pin; every other live doc is version-free and points at it') is NOT met at HEAD. Four live reference docs still carry a currency pin, and all four disagree with native-capabilities.md (which states CC v2.1.220 / Opus 5): audit-checklist.md:5 'Claude 5 family / Opus 4.8 generation, Claude Code v2.1.211'; evidence-base.md:5-6 'Claude 5 family / Opus 4.8 generation, Claude Code v2.1.211'; harness-evolution.md:19 'last-grounded: CC v2.1.211 · ... + Opus 4.8'; harness-discipline.md:5 'Claude 5 family / Opus 4.8 generation, Claude Code v2.1.210'. The strongest single instance is internal to one file: harness-discipline.md's header claims it is grounded for the Opus 4.8 generation / CC v2.1.210, while its own line 102 (added in v1.19.3/v1.19.5 — git log confirms both commits touched this file after the header stamp was last set) states Opus-5-specific runtime behaviour. That is precisely the 'two files disagree and the reader believes whichever they opened' failure the release was written to prevent, compressed into one file. Note the section contains a genuine internal tension the detector defers to a human pass: an earlier bullet says dated grounding stamps are provenance and should be KEPT, while the target-form bullet says only one live doc may carry the currency pin. These four hits sit exactly on that seam.

items.name: Independent re-derivation of shipped runtime claims (references/native-capabilities.md)
items.claims_selected: The three a consumer is most likely to act on form a hazard / boundary / workaround triple: (1) WebSearch dies at xhigh on Opus 5 — what to avoid; (2) WebSearch works at high on Opus 5 — where the safe boundary is; (3) Sonnet 5 keeps search at xhigh — the prescribed escape (`model: claude-sonnet-5`).

harness.runner: $SCRATCH/run.sh — unsets every CLAUDE* var (and AI_AGENT) so the child computes its own state, then: timeout 300 claude -p "Use the WebSearch tool exactly once to search for: Anthropic Claude Code release notes. Then reply with just the number of results you got. Use no other tool." --model $MODEL --effort $EFFORT --allowedTools WebSearch --output-format stream-json --verbose </dev/null > runs/$LABEL.jsonl
harness.env_hygiene_verified: for v in $(env | grep -oE '^CLAUDE[A-Za-z_]*' | sort -u); do unset "$v"; done  ->  'env | grep -c CLAUDE' returned 0
oracles: primary: the API rejection text, which self-reports the tier actually in force — grep -o "output_config.effort '[a-z]*'"
control: grep -c '"name":"WebSearch"' — proves the tool was actually invoked, so a 'pass' is never just a skipped call

tier readback: the transcript's per-message effort field under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl — the independent oracle for the rows that PASS, where no rejection text exists to name the tier
harness.confounder_controlled: The operator's user-level ~/.claude/settings.json pins effortLevel:"xhigh". For the passing Opus row this is a real confound, closed by the transcript readback: the --effort high run recorded effort "high" x3, i.e. the launch flag overrode settings downward. All result files are my own; none were reused.
harness.runs: 6 (2 per row for the three claims) + 1 bonus row at max

results.claim: 1 — Opus 5 at xhigh: WebSearch fails with 400 quoting the tier
results.shipped_row: | xhigh | effortLevel in settings / --effort xhigh | fails 3/3, 4/4, 3/3 |
results.observed: 2/2 FAILED. WebSearch invoked 1/1 in each (control passes). Rejection body verbatim: "API Error: 400 output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported when thinking is disabled on this model. Use effort 'high' or below, or enable thinking." Transcript per-message effort read "xhigh" x5 in both.

results.shipped_row: | high | --effort high, claude-opus-5[1m] | ok 0/2 — returned 7 results |
results.observed: 2/2 SUCCEEDED. WebSearch invoked 1/1 in each. No output_config.effort text anywhere. Model answer: '7' plus a source list (Claude Help Center release notes, Claude Platform release notes, ...). Transcript per-message effort read "high" x3, model claude-opus-5 — so --effort high genuinely overrode the settings' xhigh.
results.verdict: CONFIRMED — and the result count matches the shipped row exactly (7 results), on claude-opus-5 rather than the 1m variant the row used

results.claim: 3 — Sonnet 5 keeps WebSearch at xhigh (the prescribed escape)
results.shipped_row: 'claude-sonnet-5 and claude-fable-5 searched cleanly — 0/8 failures ... Sonnet 5 and Fable 5 keep search at xhigh and max'
results.observed: 2/2 SUCCEEDED. WebSearch invoked 1/1 in each. No effort rejection. Answer: '7'. Transcript per-message effort read "xhigh" x4, model claude-sonnet-5.
results.verdict: CONFIRMED, and unconfounded — the transcript readback proves the tier really was xhigh, and the Opus runs in the identical harness at the same readback tier were rejected. Model is the only varied factor.
results.note: This closes a gap the shipped table leaves open: a passing row has no rejection text to name its tier, so the shipped 0/8 rests on the mechanism rather than a readback. The per-message effort field supplies that readback.

results.claim: bonus — the rejection quotes the tier actually in force, not a fixed string
results.observed: FAILED with "400 output_config.effort 'max' is not supported when thinking is disabled on this model"; transcript effort "max" x5.
results.verdict: CONFIRMED — 'xhigh' and 'max' rejections are distinct and track the tier, so the oracle is self-validating

results.claim: REFUTED sub-claim — 'it is silent ... the error text goes into the WebSearch tool_result body with no is_error flag and no API-error record'

observed.stream_json_failing_run: tool_result keys: ['content','is_error','tool_use_id','type'], is_error = True, content = "API Error: 400 output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported..."
observed.stream_json_passing_run: tool_result keys: ['content','tool_use_id','type'] — no is_error key at all

results.detail: The half of the claim about isApiErrorMessage STANDS — that field is genuinely absent, so a filter keyed on it cannot see the failure. But 'no is_error flag' is FALSE on CC 2.1.220 / Opus 5, on BOTH surfaces: the failing WebSearch tool_result carries is_error:true, and the succeeding one omits the key entirely. is_error is therefore an exact discriminator for this failure. Consumer impact is favourable and worth shipping: a harness can detect the whole class mechanically by filtering tool_result blocks where name==WebSearch and is_error==true — cheaper and more direct than the 'detection glob one level deeper than the session file' the doc currently prescribes. Secondary observation, weaker: in both failing runs the model's own final answer explicitly reported the search failure rather than returning a confident answer with a tier missing — but my prompt asked only for the result count, which makes a failure trivially noticeable, so this does not generalise to the research-delegate scenario the doc describes.

The continuity trail for those three audits exists only on this machine. Not a defect in any guard; an inconsistently applied convention.
